title: Social Media and Videos Linked to Worse Test Scores
paragraphs: The more students look at social media and online videos, the worse their test scores are.
That's what was found in a Japanese government survey from April and May 2026. It looked at sixth-grade elementary school students and third-year junior high school students.
In Japan, 95% of sixth-grade elementary school students and 99% of third-year junior high school students now have a smartphone or tablet.

And among the elementary school students, 22% spend at least four hours each weekday looking at social media or online videos. That's up from just 12% who spent this long on social media or videos in 2024 — an 84% increase.
Among the junior high school students, 29% spend more than four hours on social media or videos — up from 18% two years ago.
That's bad news for students — because those who spend this much time on social media or videos have the worst scores on national tests of Japanese, math and English.

For example, elementary school students who spend less than 30 minutes on social media or videos got the highest average on this year's math tests, at 69%. But those who spend more than four hours had the lowest average, at 48%.
The results were almost exactly the same for junior high school students.
Interestingly, students who don't have a smartphone or tablet actually had slightly worse scores than students who look at social media or videos for up to about one hour a day.
And students had better scores as they got more confident in their ability to use the internet to find information, and their ability to use devices to make documents, graphs and presentations.
This suggests that the key may be encouraging students to use devices for proactive purposes, rather than just passive things like scrolling social media and watching videos.
